title: Exact orbit contacts change an HD 139139 duration score by less than 0.01 at an 88.1-day benchmark
abstract: We test exact orbit contacts for a restricted model of the 28 known HD 139139 dips. At period 88.1 days, eccentricity 0.873844, a solar host, small objects and complete detection, the eight-bin duration score changes from 11.490 to 11.498. The mean absolute paired duration change is 5.12 seconds. Exact orientation selection and contact timing have little effect at this benchmark. Scalar contact roots, direct time integration, a circular formula and a finer integration check support the calculation. This is a fixed-parameter geometry test, not a calibrated model probability. Detection, detector defects and independent confirmation remain open. No new dip or planet is found. Source records stay external. Original code, aggregate evidence and exact retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Exact contacts and straight tracks give nearly equal expected counts at the stated benchmark. The right panel shows the small change in duration score at five eccentricities.
